comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies
comparator.academicYear: 2027–2028 year 1; 2028–2029 year 2; 2029–2030 year 3, provisional prospective pathway
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official prospective pages establish 60 EC of year-one compulsory courses; 30 EC of year-two compulsory courses and two 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors chosen by the student; and, for the ordinary non-abroad year-three pathway, 10 EC personal/professional development, 5 EC public communication, 5 EC misinformation/persuasion, 10 EC thesis and 30 EC genuine free choice. Zero-credit mentoring and academic-language elements are omitted from the credit-bearing list. The website describes optional profile directions but does not impose one named route in the displayed generic curriculum; no formal route is claimed or selected. Minor and free space are preserved rather than filled with invented courses. Radboud's official year-one CIW page currently sits under an International Business Communication URL path, but the page heading and listed Dutch CIW courses identify the exact target.

alternatives.label: Closest match to communication & information studies
alternatives.concept: A broad communication programme joining rhetoric, language and media analysis to organisational communication, marketing, digital media and empirical research. It addresses several strands of Radboud's general curriculum without reproducing its multilingual, profile-specific training or required thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines communication and media, organisational and marketing contexts, digital systems and research methods; the broad label avoids treating one strand as the whole programme.
progression: Rhetoric, business, data and research foundations precede advanced persuasion, market research, organisational psychology and digital study; all formal prerequisites are earlier and semester availability is satisfied.

alternatives.label: Communication for social impact
alternatives.concept: A public communication route connecting rhetoric and media analysis with climate, health, social movements, environmental justice and civil society. Its empirical and organisational courses support scrutiny of persuasive messages and communication for change.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed courses have sustained public, climate, health and social-justice content alongside communication theory and methods, so the social-impact label describes the curricular priority.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad programme, this route replaces nine courses in business, marketing, data and AI with climate, public health, media representation, social movements, environmental justice and civil-society study; those differences follow the evidenced social-impact direction.
progression: Introductory rhetoric, sociology, climate and public-health foundations precede analysis of environmental media, social movements, persuasion and advanced civil-society study. The research and business gateway precedes all dependent courses, and assigned terms match availability.

alternatives.label: Human and digital communication
alternatives.concept: A digital communication route examining social media, persuasive texts, human language processing and the behaviour and ethics of AI systems. It combines programming, data and visual methods with communication research while acknowledging that UCR does not offer Radboud's dedicated chatbot-evaluation course.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines rhetorical communication with media and human language study and substantial AI, programming and data analysis, so both human and digital elements are visible.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes specialised programming, AI decision-making, neural networks, visual analysis, psycholinguistics and philosophy of mind for much of the broad programme's international business, marketing, organisational psychology and qualitative-methods strand. It also differs from the social-impact route by a sustained technical and cognitive sequence.
progression: Communication, business and data foundations precede digital transformation and advanced rhetoric; mathematical methods and programming precede neural networks and AI optimisation, and brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass.

selection.assessment: The broad route covers communication, organisations, media, persuasion and research. Social impact and human/digital communication have independently evidenced organising logics and material curricular consequences; the pairs differ by nine, ten and sixteen courses respectively, exceeding the four-course floor. Multilingual/intercultural business communication is another evidenced direction but no fourth programme can be included.

blocks: Both study rhetorical argument and public discourse; UCR uses examples from contemporary media and public debate.
Both analyse how linguistic choices create meaning in texts and discourse.
Both investigate contested and persuasive public messages; UCR's particular case is climate communication.

Both examine persuasive communication through theory and research on audience effects.

notes.text: Radboud offers sustained study of multilingual organisational communication, specialist communication analysis, digital communication and a compulsory bachelor thesis. UCR can combine rhetoric, media, organisational study, social issues and digital methods in different ways, but these schedules do not replicate the full specialist sequence or required thesis.
